purpose: Define the exact boundary by which a due `#CAL` occurrence becomes an inert scheduling Event that can then participate in normal Event→Trigger→Runner causality.

topics.name: Schedule to Event Boundary
topics.purpose: Define the exact boundary by which a due `#CAL` occurrence becomes an inert scheduling Event that can then participate in normal Event→Trigger→Runner causality.

semantics.event_rule: Scheduling Event references exact schedule and occurrence identities.
semantics.payload_rule: Event payload may carry bounded schedule/occurrence metadata and remains inert.
semantics.trigger_rule: Schedule does not bypass Trigger semantics unless an explicitly declared direct operation binding contract exists in the future.
semantics.authority_rule: Due time does not grant execution authorization.
semantics.dedupe_rule: Each occurrence has deterministic identity/deduplication evidence preventing accidental duplicate emission.
semantics.failure_rule: Failure to emit/handle Event is recorded explicitly and never represented as successful downstream execution.
semantics.causality_rule: Downstream execution/results retain causality refs to originating schedule occurrence/Event.

invariants.rule: A schedule determines when a scheduling occurrence may be emitted; it never directly executes a Routine, command or operation. Execution requires the normal explicit Event→Trigger→Runner/operation causality chain.

hard_gates.condition: duplicate occurrence emitted without dedupe evidence
failed event emission shown as executed

references.purpose: Scheduled execution uses explicit causality edges.
Scheduling Events enter normal Trigger path.
